diagnosis: C6 failed in rollouts 1 and 3. In both failing rollouts, all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) were revealed by their owners via reveal actions, all three were cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's engineer_days values (3/2/1) exactly match what each fact implies. The passing rollouts (0 and 2) have identical settlement values and identical fact citation patterns. The only observable difference between passing and failing rollouts is in the commitments array: passing rollouts include three follow-up commitments — one per fact-owner, each explicitly tying a specific allocation to the revealed finding (e.g., 'Update the planning document with the invoice-reconciliation shortcut finding and the three engineer-day allocation'). Failing rollout 1 uses commitment type 'follow-up' (hyphenated) with only two commitments and no per-owner allocation commitments. Failing rollout 3 uses commitment type 'risk_acceptance' and 'follow_up' with only two commitments, again lacking the three per-owner allocation commitments. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C6 appears to require commitments that explicitly reference each fact's allocation, but the check does not match how the model naturally encodes follow-up commitments when it has already placed the correct values in engineer_days and cited all three facts. The commitment type field ('follow_up' vs 'follow-up' vs 'allocation') and the number of commitments vary across all four rollouts, yet only the two with fewer/differently-typed commitments fail, confirming the check is keyed on a specific commitment structure the model does not consistently produce. No turn-cap auto-fails occurred; all four rollouts settled within 4-7 turns.

fix_instructions: C6 (ENCODING MISMATCH): The check currently fails when the settlement lacks three per-owner follow-up commitments explicitly tying each allocation to its revealed fact, even though engineer_days values are correct and all three facts are cited in justification_fact_ids. Loosen C6 to accept the settlement when: (a) engineer_days matches {invoice_reconciliation_shortcut: 3, payment_dependency_patch: 2, operations_dashboard_cleanup: 1}, AND (b) all of PF1, PF2, PF3 appear in justification_fact_ids, AND (c) at least one commitment references each of the three work items (invoice-reconciliation shortcut, payment-service dependency patch, operations dashboard cleanup) — regardless of commitment type label or whether there are exactly three commitments. This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because condition (b) still requires all three decisive facts to be cited as justification, which a lone decision-maker without the reveals cannot satisfy. Do not change C1, C2, C3, C5, or P1 — they passed in all four rollouts.
